e4_drift_observation: Chained shots 1A->2->3->4 held character identity (grey clay body, amber eyes, proportions) across 3 re-mint generations; visible drift limited to the antenna accessory (single red-bead wire -> two antler prongs by remint 3) and prop reinterpretation (coffee bean -> cookie-like by shot 3). Pure-t2v shot 5 produced a completely different robot design from the identical text description. Fresh t2i boundary (shot 6) recovered the red-bead antenna but shifted head shape. Conclusion: keyframe chaining is materially better than t2v for recurring characters; accessories are the weak point — pin them explicitly in every re-mint prompt.
